name: agents
description: What `sbx create` and `sbx run` send for an agent beyond its kit: workspaces (several, read-only, mounted elsewhere, a single read-only file), clone mode and the git remote of the host, agent arguments, the environment and working directory of a session, skills, environment, ports and deny rules at creation, and a governance profile. Shell kit only.

scenarios.name: create-w-workspaces
scenarios.note: the primary workspace, a read-only one, one mounted elsewhere, and a single file held read-only inside the primary workspace

scenarios.name: exec-w-mounts
args: pwd; grep -E 'mountdir|docs|data' /proc/mounts | cut -d' ' -f2,4; touch {fixtures}/docs/written 2>&1; echo written >> {fixtures}/mountdir/hello.txt 2>&1; echo written > /workspace/data/written 2>&1 && echo data-writable
scenarios.note: where each workspace lands and which ones the sandbox can write

scenarios.name: git-init
scenarios.note: a host repository for clone mode; the identity and settings of the user are kept out of its commit

scenarios.name: git-remote-c
scenarios.note: the sandbox-<name> remote the CLI adds to the host repository

scenarios.name: git-config-c
scenarios.note: how the remote reaches the sandbox: its URL, refspecs and upload-pack command

scenarios.name: exec-c-commit
args: pwd; git log --oneline -1; git -c user.name=agent -c user.email=agent@example.invalid -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q --allow-empty -m 'agent work' && git log --oneline -1; grep -E 'sandbox/source' /proc/mounts | cut -d' ' -f2,4
scenarios.note: the clone inside the sandbox: where it is, its history, a commit of the agent, and the read-only source

scenarios.name: git-fetch-c
scenarios.note: the commit of the agent comes back through the remote: what the fetch sends to the daemon

scenarios.name: git-remote-after-rm
scenarios.note: whether removing the sandbox removes its remote

scenarios.name: run-r-flag-args
scenarios.note: agent arguments starting with a flag: added to the default command of the kit

scenarios.name: run-r-command-args
scenarios.note: agent arguments starting with a word: they replace the default command

scenarios.name: run-r-env-workdir
scenarios.note: environment and working directory of one session

scenarios.name: run-r-tty
args: echo TERM=$TERM COLORTERM=$COLORTERM TZ=$TZ; stty size
scenarios.note: a session on a terminal: what the CLI passes from the host

scenarios.name: create-s-options
scenarios.note: skills, environment, a published port and a deny rule chosen at creation

scenarios.name: create-k-skills-readwrite
scenarios.note: the other explicit skills mode; the shell kit has no skills directory

scenarios.name: create-p-profile-unknown
scenarios.note: a governance profile that does not exist: documents the field and the error
